meta.title: Does the grid bind?
meta.subject: What Happens When Chip Volume Doubles but the Grid Does Not
meta.author: Dean Lee

claims.text: Huang: NVIDIA will sell twice as many chips next year
claims.note: True, but he said “chips” and never defined the basket. No primary source narrows it to data-centre GPUs.

claims.text: NVIDIA outlined FY2028 revenue of roughly $673 billion
claims.note: Not NVIDIA’s number. CNBC’s arithmetic on an analyst consensus. “673” appears zero times in the 8-K, the 10-Q and the transcript.

claims.text: The thirty-point gap implies ASP compression
claims.note: −15%, not −30. Different speakers, dates and periods. And NVIDIA attributed the gap to supply on that same call.

claims.text: Fab and packaging capacity can double within several quarters
claims.note: True in 2024. CoWoS growth now decays to +30%. TSMC’s CEO: “two to three years to build a new fab. No shortcuts.”

claims.text: High-voltage transformers carry 36–48 month lead times
claims.note: Directionally right, high, and thin. Best survey figure is 29 months; every published number traces to one root.

claims.text: Interconnection queues average four to seven years
claims.note: Measured median request-to-COD is 61 months for 2025 completions.

claims.text: The grid cannot double energized megawatts in twelve months
claims.note: ERCOT energized +0.9 GW of large load in 2025 against 445.8 GW of applications.

claims.text: Excess hardware takes one of two paths, both penalised
claims.note: It is three regimes, not two, with a computable boundary. Verified exhaustively in TLA+.

claims.text: Accelerators halve in competitiveness within three to four years
claims.note: A 2020-vintage A100 is appreciating. NVIDIA disclosed A100 rental up ~15% year on year.

claims.text: Hyperscalers extended server life, deferring billions
claims.note: $43.8bn of FY2025 operating income across five companies — 11% of what they reported.
Confirmed — and it already happened. Amazon took a $920M charge in Q4 2024. But the conclusion inverts.

claims.text: Marginal cost is largely electricity; spot prices must fall
claims.note: Electricity is 20% of cash cost. Spot is up 32.5% off its trough — the same datum that confirms C13, because the two claims are about different things: the average and the variance.

Initially scored partial here, against the wrong test — whether the market sits inside the loss band. C13 is a claim about DISPERSION between holders of energized interconnection and holders of unenergized hardware, and that rent migration is observable. Corrected after the author pointed it out.

regimes.name: Absorption is free
regimes.body: New capacity arrives faster than hardware does. Nothing is stranded and nothing is written down.

regimes.name: The write-down is forced
regimes.body: Everything can be racked, but only by pulling working gear out of the envelope it occupies. There is no clean schedule.

regimes.name: Stranding is forced
regimes.body: No operator strategy absorbs the programme. Cannibalising does not cure it — it adds a write-down to it. The article misses this case.

sobol.k: Share landing in an energized envelope

density_refresh.ceiling_note: A third limit applies on top: a hall's feeders, busway and local substation are sized for the density it was built at, so freeing 140 kW across fourteen cabinets does not put 140 kW at one cabinet. Raised by the author in reply. No published figure exists for how much retrofit in-building distribution permits, so the bound above is a ceiling rather than a level.

unknowns: What fraction of new hardware lands in an already-energized envelope. No published measurement. 33.9% of the variance.
What fraction is powered outside the interconnection queue. No published measurement. 33.9% of the variance.
Fleet-weighted GPU utilization. Measured values span 5% to 85%. No one has published a weighted average.
What Amazon actually retired in Q4 2024 — no generation, count, location or gross cost is disclosed.
Burry’s $176bn derivation. Verified as his exact words; the method is paywalled and unreproduced in ten months.
The scaling from two published meter readings to a national energization figure. No source provides it — and it carries the verdict.

How much retrofit capacity in-building distribution actually permits — feeders, busway and the local substation. Raised by the author after publication; searched, and it returns the same confirmed negative as decommissioned megawatts. A third unsourced quantity on top of the two above.
